sanity_expectations: For fixed c0, p_trigger, and rho, c_eff should remain close to c0 when p is well below p_trigger, then decline smoothly rather than discontinuously as p passes through the neighborhood of p_trigger.

For fixed c0, p_trigger, and rho with rho>0, increasing p from just above p_trigger to substantially above p_trigger should generally decrease c_eff, with stronger suppression deeper in the active regime.
For fixed p, p_trigger, and rho, c_eff scales linearly with c0; therefore c_eff/c0 should be invariant to changing c0.
For fixed c0, p, and p_trigger, increasing rho should not increase c_eff; it should weakly decrease c_eff, with almost no effect when p is far below trigger.

Distinguishing-condition check: compare samples with the same ratio p/p_trigger but different absolute p values while holding c0 and rho fixed; this law predicts different c_eff/c0 because the factor exp(-p/p_trigger) enters separately, so equal relative exceedance need not imply equal controlled-contact fraction.
Because p_trigger>0 throughout the design, all evaluated outputs should remain finite and real on the sampled grid.

rationale: The analyzed expression is a static explicit relation solvable for c_eff with no derivatives, no integrals, and no hidden state, so exact input-output evaluation is appropriate. Because the record carries an explicit freedom decision of none and all four non-target symbols were declared as sampled inputs, preserve p, c0, p_trigger, and rho as independent sampled axes rather than fixing any as parameters. Chosen ranges keep the formula finite and real and respect the biologic interpretation: prevalence p is a fraction, trigger p_trigger is positive and smaller than the upper prevalence bound, rho is a bounded suppression fraction, and c0 is a plausible baseline contact rate. The p_trigger lower bound stays away from zero to avoid singular behavior in p/p_trigger and (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger. The selected ranges intentionally expose the recorded distinguishing conditions: (i) p spans below-trigger, near-trigger, and well-above-trigger values for many p_trigger values, revealing the smoothed activation band from the tanh gate; (ii) p and p_trigger vary independently so cases with similar relative exceedance and different absolute p are present, allowing the added absolute-prevalence factor exp(-p/p_trigger) to alter c_eff/c0; (iii) rho varies away from 0 and 1 so suppression is visible but not trivially absent or saturated; (iv) c0 varies to scale the output while leaving the normalized suppression structure checkable. Some sampled combinations will be in weak-effect regions such as p far below p_trigger or rho small; these are scientifically admissible and useful for preserving the inactive branch and showing that suppression vanishes continuously near low prevalence. The main observable contrast is strongest when p is near to moderately above p_trigger and when comparing pairs with similar p/p_trigger but different absolute p and nontrivial rho.
